strengths: Well-motivated identification of critic staleness as a real problem in on-policy critique-guided RL with clear articulation of why static critics become misaligned with evolving failure patterns
Convincing empirical demonstration of failure-pattern drift (RQ2) using t-SNE visualization across four diverse environments, showing genuine distributional shift rather than just error reduction
Comprehensive experimental evaluation with consistent improvements (~7.3 points average over GRPO) across four benchmarks and generalization across backbone sizes (4B-7B)

Principled saturation-aware reward design with three desirable mathematical properties (saturation-aware, additive/path-consistent, antisymmetric) and effective visualization of benefits in high-score regime (Figure 4)
Clear presentation with effective visualizations, complete pseudocode (Algorithm 1), and comprehensive appendices including implementation details and case studies
Meaningful ablation studies demonstrating individual component contributions
weaknesses: Limited conceptual novelty—primarily combines existing techniques (GRPO, cascaded rollouts, gain shaping) rather than introducing fundamental new methods; co-evolution of policy-critic is not novel

Insufficient isolation of staleness effect: RQ2 compares frozen critic to ECHO but doesn't control for the update mechanism; missing comparisons to asynchronous critic updates or alternative update frequencies

Saturation-aware reward ω(s) = 1/(1-s+η) lacks theoretical justification—choice of this specific functional form over alternatives (exponential, power functions) is not justified; smoothing parameter η=0.1 set uniformly with no sensitivity analysis

Experimental rigor concerns: no confidence intervals or significance testing despite visible variance in training curves (Figure 5); unclear if results are single-run or multi-seed averaged; Table 2 ablations only on 2/4 environments for SA reward component

Acknowledged but unaddressed critical dependency on reward quality: both policy and critic learn from same reward model, creating compounding error if rewards are noisy/biased; no robustness experiments provided

Missing computational efficiency analysis: cascaded rollout requires N critiques + N refinements per query (N=8 default), substantially increasing inference cost; no wall-clock time or training efficiency comparisons provided

Design choices lack justification: default group size N=8 has no ablation study; same-backbone initialization for policy and critic may limit specialization; no investigation of architecture alternatives

Incomplete related work engagement: limited discussion of co-evolutionary learning and evolutionary algorithms literature; sparse coverage of curriculum learning and meta-learning approaches that address similar adaptation problems

strengths: Well-motivated problem: clearly identifies critic staleness as a practical issue in on-policy critique-guided RL
Comprehensive experiments: 4 diverse environments with consistent improvements (7.28 pts average over GRPO), competitive with much larger models
Strong empirical evidence of failure-pattern drift: t-SNE visualization in Section 5.2.1 effectively shows non-stationary failure modes across training phases
Principled reward design: saturation-aware gain shaping is mathematically sound with desirable properties (additive, antisymmetric, saturation-aware)
Good ablation on frozen critics: Table 2 and Figure 5 provide evidence that co-evolution is beneficial, with phase-dependent analysis
Reproducibility: includes pseudo-code, hyperparameters, and reasonable implementation detail coverage
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: combines existing components (cascaded rollouts, GRPO, saturation-aware rewards) with relatively incremental contribution; insufficient for strong acceptance at top venues
Unaddressed circular optimization: both policy and critic optimize using same reward model R; if R is biased, both drift toward exploiting those biases; no analysis of this compounding-error risk
Critical reward-model dependency under-explored: major limitation (acknowledged but not experimentally validated); no robustness analysis for noisy/biased rewards; unclear how R is obtained
Incomplete ablation studies: saturation-aware reward ablated on only 2/4 environments; no ablation on cascade size N, rollout mechanism itself, or alternative update frequencies for critic

Causality not rigorously established: while failure-pattern drift is shown and frozen critics underperform, mechanistic link is not proven; unclear if improvements come from co-evolution vs. simply having multiple diverse critiques
Arbitrary design choices: specific log-barrier form for saturation weighting not justified; η=0.1 fixed without sensitivity analysis; behavior near saturation (s→1) could be unstable
Lack of statistical rigor: no error bars, confidence intervals, or significance testing; appears to be single runs; concerning for stochastic RL setting
No human evaluation: critiques not assessed for quality; entire evaluation on automated metrics; no verification that critique utility actually increases during training
Generalization under-explored: only Qwen models tested; policy/critic always use same backbone; missing ablations on different model sizes and sensitivity to N
Incomplete comparisons: no direct empirical comparison with RCO (Yu et al. 2025) or CTRL (Xie et al. 2025) despite close similarity; distinctions from prior work unclear

strengths: Well-motivated problem: The identification of 'critic staleness' in on-policy RL is compelling and well-articulated, with effective empirical demonstration through failure-pattern drift visualization in Section 5.2.1

Comprehensive experimental evaluation: Testing across 4 diverse environments with strong baselines (proprietary and open-source), multiple model sizes, and consistent improvements (7.28 points average over GRPO)
Strong empirical results: Notable gains on DeepSearch (42% relative improvement) and WebShop (9% relative improvement), with competitive performance against much larger models

Solid technical approach: Saturation-aware gain shaping is theoretically motivated with desirable properties (saturation-aware, additive, antisymmetric); cascaded rollout mechanism is well-designed for group-structured trajectories
Thorough ablation studies: Table 2 and Figure 5 provide convincing evidence for the importance of critic evolution, with phase-dependent analysis adding nuance to the findings
Reproducibility efforts: Detailed pseudocode (Algorithm 1), implementation details, hyperparameter specifications, and case studies demonstrate strong care for reproducibility
Clear presentation: Effective use of Figure 1 for paradigm comparison and well-structured methodology section with good visualizations
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: Cascaded rollouts are straightforward, group-relative advantage estimation is from prior work (GRPO), and saturation-aware reward shaping is an incremental contribution; main novelty is the co-evolutionary combination, which feels more engineering-focused

Critical dependence on external reward model: All training signals rely on a single reward model R, and the paper lacks analysis of robustness to reward noise, bias, or misspecification; this severely limits practical applicability
Missing statistical rigor: No confidence intervals, significance testing, or number of seeds/runs reported; design choices (N=8, η=0.1) lack ablation studies or justification
Incomplete experimental analysis: SciWorld ablation for SA-aware is missing (Table 2); unclear if comparisons use equivalent compute budgets; no direct measurement of critique quality improvement

Generalization concerns: Results limited to simulated LLM agent environments on academic benchmarks; critic prompting template (Box A.1) is task-specific; unclear how method scales to real-world settings
Unexplained performance gaps: DeepSearch shows ECHO at 47.25 vs. GPT-5 at 72.19; why ECHO underperforms here is not discussed; smallest improvements on SciWorld (~3.7 points) lack explanation

Methodological limitations: Frozen critic ablation doesn't isolate staleness from distribution shift effects; no comparison of saturation functions; score-aware conditioning might produce trivial feedback when so is high

Missing comparisons: No direct comparison with CTRL (cited as related work); no evaluation of alternative reward shaping approaches; computational cost analysis missing despite requiring N×2 forward passes per query

strengths: Well-motivated problem with strong empirical demonstration: The paper convincingly demonstrates failure-pattern drift during training and shows that frozen critics become stale, addressing a genuine limitation in existing critique-guided RL approaches.

Consistent and substantial experimental improvements: ECHO shows gains across all four diverse environments (WebShop +9%, ALFWorld +4%, SciWorld +5%, DeepSearch +42%), with results generalizing across model sizes.

Thorough and rigorous experimental evaluation: Comprehensive ablation studies (Table 2), analysis of critique-refinement alignment and granularity evolution (Table 6), controlled comparisons isolating critic effects (Table 5), and detailed training time breakdown showing manageable 15% overhead.

Technically sound approach with well-designed components: The saturation-aware reward function (Eq. 6) has desirable mathematical properties (saturation-awareness, additivity, antisymmetry), and the cascaded rollout mechanism is practical and clearly described.

Excellent presentation and reproducibility: Clear writing with informative figures, detailed implementation details in appendices, full prompts, and complete algorithmic description in pseudocode format.
weaknesses: Limited algorithmic novelty: The contribution primarily combines existing techniques (multi-view sampling, GRPO, group-relative advantages). Individual components are incremental—cascaded rollouts are common in ensemble methods, GRPO is prior work, and saturation-aware reward applies standard reward shaping principles.

Insufficient analysis of critical reward model dependency: While the framework heavily depends on external reward quality, exploration is limited—no robustness analysis for noisy/biased rewards, no sensitivity analysis for η (fixed at 0.1), and reward misalignment risks are only briefly mentioned in limitations.

Incomplete baseline comparisons: Missing comparison with simpler alternatives (periodic critic retraining). RCO comparison is somewhat unfair since RCO doesn't update the policy. Limited comparison with other recent training-based critics beyond RCO and LUFFY.

Saturation-aware reward design lacks strong justification: The choice of log-barrier functional form appears arbitrary without exploring design space. Only ablated on 2 of 4 environments (binary-reward tasks excluded). Performance drop without SA is modest (3.84 points), questioning its importance.

Limited characterization of when critic co-evolution is beneficial: No analysis of task properties determining when synchronized updates help most. Unclear if method benefits domains with static failure patterns or when periodic retraining would suffice. Environment-dependent effects (e.g., RQ3) suggest task-specificity deserving more investigation.

Missing important ablations and sensitivity analyses: No ablation on score-aware conditioning (Eq. 1), group size N=8 not justified or studied, no exploration of update synchronization schemes (simultaneous vs. sequential). Limited sensitivity analysis for key hyperparameters.

Statistical rigor concerns: No error bars, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Unclear if results from single runs or averages. Some baseline models not reproducible. Makes it difficult to assess result reliability.

Incomplete characterization of critic staleness: While Figure 3 shows failure pattern drift, direct measurement of frozen critic quality degradation is missing. Connection between drift and frozen critic underperformance could be more explicit, particularly when frozen critic severely underperforms even standard GRPO.
